question: Should the agent use the actual representations of unlabelled task inputs when deciding which frozen encoder deserves its next experiment? Today its exploration utility estimates similarity from executable descriptions and past scores.
source: Use the previously registered pair of small/large primary training runs in the fidelity archive. Include one fitted pipeline per distinct encoder that was observed in both runs, selected without reading evaluation scores by the lowest executable configuration digest. The panel is conditioned on methods that the historic search actually trained. The two training sizes are not independent tasks.
probe: Select one comparison per connected component on the SMALL fitting split in order of a fixed hash of unordered strings; take the first 96. This subset is outside both held panels. Obtain the actual frozen vector function from the retained pipeline, form the signed unit vector difference of the two texts, and compute centered linear kernel alignment on the same 96 comparisons. Use no fitting labels to calculate these similarities. Reference https://proceedings.mlr.press/v97/kornblith19a.html
policy: Hold the next action type fixed to exploration. At both training sizes split the primary held rows by connected component into two feedback/evaluation roles, and rotate. For each unordered pair of distinct encoders as already observed history, call the existing exploration utility twice. Control uses the original description-based similarity. Alternative averages that similarity with measured task geometry, equal weights fixed in advance. All priors, action sorting, measured feedback, feasible alternatives and fit costs are identical. Each may nominate exactly one next experiment. Reuse its archived feedback only after nomination; elect the best single or equal pair from the three observed models on the feedback role and score it on the other groups. No new supervised base fits. This is a one-step counterfactual, never evidence of a full autonomous run.
gate: Report how often a next choice changed and mean held correct-count difference per opportunity for each size. Eligibility for a real scheduler trial requires at least 10% changed choices and at least +0.2 percentage points average improvement on both sizes, with neither evaluation-role average negative. The same held examples occur in multiple counterfactuals; do not sum them as unique recovered course questions.
budget: Zero new encoder/classifier fits, zero API calls. The discrete simulated feedback choices are counted separately. No course-designated validation, official test or H2.
